Prior density

Source: R/priors-density.R
density.prior.Rd

Computes density of a prior distribution across a range of values.

# S3 method for class 'prior'
density(
  x,
  x_seq = NULL,
  x_range = NULL,
  x_range_quant = NULL,
  n_points = 1000,
  n_samples = 10000,
  force_samples = FALSE,
  individual = FALSE,
  transformation = NULL,
  transformation_arguments = NULL,
  transformation_settings = FALSE,
  truncate_end = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

a prior

x_seq

sequence of x coordinates

x_range

vector of length two with lower and upper display limits (used if x_seq is unspecified)

x_range_quant

quantile used for automatically obtaining x_range if both x_range and x_seq are unspecified. A number in the open interval (0, 0.5); other values are refused. Defaults to 0.005 for all but Cauchy, Student-t, Gamma, inverse-gamma, moment, and inverse-moment distributions that use 0.010.

n_points

number of equally spaced points in the x_range if x_seq is unspecified

n_samples

number of samples from the prior distribution if the density cannot be obtained analytically (or if samples are forced with force_samples = TRUE)

force_samples

should prior be sampled instead of obtaining analytic solution whenever possible. For supported ordered mixed measures, exact analytic curves and atoms are retained and the requested samples are attached to each component. Supported scalar ordered literal point totals and mixtures whose total components are all literal points do not sample, store draws, or advance the RNG when force_samples = FALSE. With force_samples = TRUE, their original seeded draws are attached without replacing the analytic measure. Other ordered families retain their existing sampling fallback.

individual

should individual densities be returned (e.g., in case of weightfunction)

transformation

transformation to be applied to the prior distribution. Either a character specifying one of the prepared transformations:

lin

linear transformation in form of a + b*x

tanh

hyperbolic tangent transformation

exp

exponential transformation

, or a list containing the transformation function fun, inverse transformation function inv, and derivative of the transformation jac, evaluated on the original support. A custom transformation can also declare output_support = c(lower, upper). Display grids on the transformed scale are evaluated only within these bounds; a wider plotting range is retained without extending the density. Infinite inverse values at support boundaries are omitted from continuous density grids. Point masses retain their transformed locations.

transformation_arguments

a list with named arguments for the transformation

transformation_settings

boolean indicating whether the explicitly supplied x_seq or x_range is on the transformed scale. Automatically selected prior-coordinate ranges are always obtained on the source scale before the density family's existing transformation handling.

truncate_end

whether the density should be set to zero for endpoints of truncated distributions

...

additional arguments

Value

density.prior returns an object of class 'density'. For Dirichlet simplex priors it returns a named list of beta-marginal density objects, one for each simplex coordinate. Ordered priors return one component per factor level. When a level has both discrete and continuous probability, its atoms table stores exact location and mass values, while its continuous table stores a density already weighted to integrate to the remaining continuous mass over its full support. A clipped plotting grid preserves density heights; diagnostics$continuous_integral reports its numerical trapezoid integral, which can differ from the exact continuous mass because of clipping and grid discretization. Nonfinite continuous ordinates are omitted by the structural mixed-measure route; the curve is not renormalized. A supported scalar point total times a random allocation share has a continuous scaled-Beta distribution at intermediate levels, with declared atoms retained for zero-total branches, reference levels, fixed shares, and the full-total level. A spike-and-slab prior returns a list of class density.prior.spike_and_slab with the slab density (variable) and the density of the spike at zero (inclusion), each scaled by its prior mass. Under a transformation, a prior with inclusion probability 1 has no prior mass in the spike, returns inclusion = NULL, and does not require a representable image of the spike location (for example log(0)); any other inclusion probability does.

Details

Sample-based density estimates for continuous priors with finite support use boundary-reflected kernel density estimates. The plotting range controls the evaluation grid, while reflection is based on the prior's true truncation bounds. Automatic transformed prior-coordinate ranges keep the existing source range and equally spaced source grid. Where the existing marginal and transformed density route supports it, a source display endpoint with an infinite transformed image uses the prior's existing marginal tail quantile, controlled by x_range_quant. Prior-list plots use the union of participating component marginal quantiles. This is a finite display window; the prior support, density, probability masses and mixture weights are unchanged. Invalid atom images remain unavailable. When an endpoint quantile is unavailable or its transformed image is still not finite (for example the 0.995 quantile of a very wide prior under "exp"), the automatic display range of the transformed prior is unavailable: density() stops with BayesTools_prior_range_unavailable, parent BayesTools_transformation_domain and BayesTools_transformation, with call = NULL, and the message names the remedy of explicit display limits (x_range or x_seq; xlim in the plotting functions). In plot_posterior() only the prior curve is omitted, with a warning of class BayesTools_prior_curve_unavailable (see there), and the posterior is drawn alone. Explicit source or transformed coordinates keep their supplied interpretation. Individual weightfunction and ordered routes retain their existing transformation behavior and conditions. Nonindividual PET/PEESE standard-error axes and weightfunction p-value axes retain their specialized interpretation. Declared point locations and finite builtin support bounds must have representable images. Finite-source exponential underflow, tanh saturation, positive-power underflow and nonfinite point images stop with BayesTools_transformation_image_unavailable, parent BayesTools_transformation, with call = NULL and fields transformation, source_values, and images for the matched failing finite sources. True zero under positive powers and infinite mathematical support limits retain their meaning. Continuous display grids retain their existing handling. Direct ordered Dirichlet-product densities use stable log-share arithmetic for literal, untruncated Normal totals with mean zero and finite positive SD, retaining the existing quadrature budget and tolerances. This guarded route does not certify tiny or nonrepresentable ranges. Every other total takes the same quadrature at each display value and accepts it when it converges within its tolerances and exceeds the absolute tolerance (the integral of a total concentrated away from zero can miss the band where the integrand is positive and give zero); the display values it does not accept take the structural route of the level (its total times a Beta share), built without a numerical grid. A quadrature that does not converge is not repeated for the rest of the level. Small second Beta shapes remain a numerical risk of the quadrature. A display value whose density neither the quadrature nor the route resolves (an NA height inside the support) is left out of the level and reported by a warning of class BayesTools_prior_curve_unavailable with the fields unresolved_values, structural_values (the limits at support ends without a structural classification, which are not warned about) and levels.
